title: Oxidation Number and Rules for Assigning It
topicTitle: Oxidation number and rules for assigning oxidation number
notes: **Oxidation number (ON):** a bookkeeping device that tracks electron transfer in a reaction. It is the charge an atom would have if all bonds were ionic.

**Rules:** (1) elemental form: ON = 0; (2) monatomic ions: ON = ionic charge; (3) oxygen: usually -2 (except peroxides -1, superoxides -1/2, with F); (4) hydrogen: +1 (except with metals: -1); (5) sum of ON in neutral compound = 0; in polyatomic ion = ion charge.
**Fluorine exception:** fluorine is always -1 because it is the most electronegative element.
**Carbon oxidation states:** range from -4 in $CH_4$ to +4 in $CO_2$. The ON of C in organic compounds is calculated from H=+1, O=-2, and halogens=-1.
**Why it matters:** oxidation numbers identify which atoms are oxidized and reduced, allow balancing of redox equations, and predict redox behaviour.
